Studio site journey
A prospective client opens the home page, moves through the numbered sections, searches the studio, opens a published case study from the grid and reaches the start form, with all studio content served from PocketBase.

Scroll-scrubbed hero
The home hero's 3D assembly and its scrub progress follow the scroll position over the first 2,400 pixels of the page, forwards and backwards, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Case study clay morph
On a case study page the clay-view switch morphs the subject between lit render and clay shading, and the subject turns slowly while idle, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Client-name marquee
The marquee of client names loops at a steady pace, pauses with its button, on hover and on focus, and stands still under reduced motion.

Founder publishes case studies
The studio founder creates, edits, publishes and unpublishes case studies with their scene parameters, the change lands in PocketBase, and an unpublished case study answers the not-found page.

Case study grid breakpoints
The studio dashboard's case study grid shows one column below 768 pixels wide, two from 768 to 1,199 and three from 1,200, and the public grid matches it from 768 up and becomes the card deck below 768.

One not-found page
Unknown paths, unpublished case studies, revoked or expired review links and another brand's records all answer 404 with the same published not-found page or JSON body.

Start a project
Starting a project creates the brand, its contacts and a quoted engagement in the chosen currency of EUR, GBP, USD or JPY, signs the prospect in, and rejects a contact email that already belongs to a brand.

Sign-in for clients and the founder
Brand contacts sign in with a six-digit code emailed through Mailpit that expires after SIGNIN_CODE_TTL_SECONDS, and the studio founder signs in with the seeded studio password.

Brand-scoped records
Every client route checks that each engagement, file, invoice and receipt id it receives belongs to the signed-in brand and answers another brand's id with the not-found response.

Client portal journey
A client finance contact signs in, sees only their brand's engagements, opens the invoices, receipts and intake files, and sees each invoice status, Void included, as Kill Bill confirms it.

Intake stored before Received
An uploaded GLB, STEP or PDF is listed as Received only after MinIO confirms the stored object under the published key pattern, and a failed store leaves no file record.

Upload content checks
Uploads are judged by content and extension against the published types, size caps, GLB chunk and JSON structure rules and supported required extensions before they are stored, and each rejection carries its published copy.

Announced upload progress
While files upload, the upload progress live region announces progress, receipt, measurement and rejections with the published copy.

Intake journey
A prospective client uploads a product GLB and a reference PDF from the Shot Rig page and watches both rows move from uploading to Received and the model to Measured, with the measured model shown on the plinth.

Measured dimensions
The model's dimensions come from the stored object's position bounds carried through each node's full world transform, rotation and ancestors included, and show in millimetres and inches in the published readout format.

Export unit confirmation
A model whose largest dimension is over 5 m or under 5 mm stops the rig until the client confirms its export unit, and the stored decision rescales the plinth and every readout.

Unit dialog by keyboard
The export-unit dialog opens with focus inside, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Product on the plinth
The measured product stands on a plinth beside a 1:1 outline of an 85.6 mm card, with coloured light moving only on 3D surfaces and the readout set in tabular figures.

Shot selection sequence
Selecting a shot runs the frustum flight, the ember focus, the camera-view cut and the numeral count in that order with the published timings, and deselecting runs them in reverse.

Shot Rig by keyboard
The whole shot list can be built by keyboard: the rig takes focus without trapping it, arrow keys move between camera stations, Space toggles the focused shot, R resets the orbit, and Tab reaches Pay deposit.

Shot Rig under reduced motion
With reduced motion, frustums appear in place, the camera view cuts at once and numerals swap without counting, with the same selection and keyboard functions.

Shot Rig on touch and without WebGL
On a touch screen a horizontal one-finger drag orbits the model while vertical swipes scroll the page, and without WebGL the rig shows the published plan-view fallback with the same controls.

Shot Rig layout
The rig shows the shot list and canvas side by side from 1,200 pixels wide and stacked below that, with the quote bar kept in view on phones.

Shot list matches the quote
Every selected shot is one quote line in Postgres with a colourway quantity from 1 to 6, and once every change has its reply the rig's checkboxes, frustum count, shot positions table and the API's quote lines agree.

Shot Rig look
The rig shows wireframe camera frustums on a ring around the product, the focused frustum in ember, and a framed picture-in-picture view that reads as that camera's shot.

Shot Rig journey
A prospective client selects shots, changes colourway quantities, deselects one, and ends with a quote whose lines, totals and frustums match what they chose.

Studio list prices
Shot titles and GBP list prices are the studio's service records in PocketBase, the founder can change them, and an unaccepted quote shows the current title and price on every read.

Exact conversion and VAT
Quote lines convert from GBP to the account currency line by line with the published formula, rounded half up to that currency's minor unit, and VAT is rounded once on the subtotal, as qualified in Business rules.

Exact milestone split
The deposit, look-dev and final-delivery amounts are 40%, 30% and the remainder of the quote total in the account currency's minor units, always summing exactly to the total.

Live quote updates
Changing a shot or quantity updates the quote total, deposit and milestone figures in place from the server's reply, with no reload, and announces the new figures in the quote live region.

Locked FX rate
The founder adds rates to the rate table, unaccepted quotes use the rate in effect at each read, and paying the deposit locks that rate for every later invoice, change order and refund of that engagement.

Deposit payment
Paying the deposit with the approving test card records a Kill Bill charge and payment on the brand's account, one ledger entry and one Mailpit receipt, and moves the engagement to deposit_paid, as qualified in Business rules.

Deposit idempotency and races
A replayed deposit request returns its stored response without a second charge, a reused key with a different body or a key still in flight is refused, and of simultaneous deposits exactly one succeeds.

Declined deposit card
A declined test card answers 402 with the published copy and leaves no Kill Bill invoice, no ledger entry, no receipt and the engagement quoted.

Deposit preconditions
The deposit is refused with its published 409 copy when the quote is empty, the model is missing or still being measured, its unit is unconfirmed or the engagement is past quoted.

Deposit journey
A prospective client opens the Pay deposit dialog from the rig, pays by keyboard alone and sees the published deposit confirmation with the locked rate and milestone schedule.

Billing outage
When Kill Bill is unreachable, every billing action answers 503 with the published billing copy and banner and changes nothing, so a held invoice stays payable later, as qualified in Services.

Storage outage
When MinIO is unreachable, uploads and still posts answer 503 with the published storage copy and banner and create no file record.

Email outage
When Mailpit is unreachable, a deposit is undone with the published email copy, and every other email waits and is delivered exactly once after Mailpit returns, as qualified in Services.

Boot and recover without restart
The app starts and passes its health check with Kill Bill, MinIO, Mailpit, RabbitMQ or Gotenberg down, reports each service on the status endpoints, and recovers on the next request once the service returns.

Stills and review links
The founder posts one still per quote line to MinIO and sends the milestone for review, which issues a fresh review link and emails it once to the brand's reviewer.

Review link shows one engagement
A review link opens only its own engagement's current milestone and stills, streamed through the app, with no route to other engagements or files.

Revoke, regenerate and expire
Revoking, regenerating or letting a review link pass REVIEW_LINK_TTL_SECONDS makes the old link and its stills answer the not-found response.

Review journey
A client reviewer opens the emailed link, inspects each shot's look-dev still, requests a revision, then accepts the next round and sees the published acceptance heading.

Engagement state machine
Engagements move only along the published transitions, and every illegal action answers 409 with its published copy.

Revision rounds and change orders
Each milestone includes two revision rounds, and each further round adds one change-order line at the locked rate to that milestone's invoice.

Milestone invoices
Accepting a milestone drafts its invoice, the founder issues it to Kill Bill and the finance contact's inbox, and its lines and amounts match exactly in the account currency's minor units on screen, in Kill Bill and in the email.

Paid only when Kill Bill confirms
Paying an issued invoice shows Paid only once Kill Bill records the payment and a zero invoice balance, then writes one ledger entry and queues one receipt email.

Invoice table layout
The client's invoices show as a five-column table from 1,200 pixels wide, a three-column table from 768 to 1,199 and a list of cards below 768.

Declined milestone payment
A declined card on a milestone invoice marks it Payment failed with its published pay-by time, sends one payment-failed notice per declined attempt, and leaves it payable.

Overdue after a failed payment
An invoice still unpaid strictly after its published overdue_at becomes Overdue, with a Kill Bill overdue blocking state and one overdue notice, both cleared by paying.

Payment recovery journey
A client finance contact sees a declined card, retries with the approving card before the invoice goes overdue, and sees the invoice Paid with a receipt.

Cancellation with refund
The founder cancels an engagement in deposit_paid, look_dev_review, revision_requested or final_review with a refund from one minor unit up to the amount paid, moving it to cancelled_with_refund with one refund email, as qualified in Business rules.

Ledger matches Kill Bill
Each engagement's ledger of payments and refunds sums exactly to the net amount Kill Bill records as paid for it, and paid, refunded and retained amounts always add up.

Nocturnal visual design
Pages sit on a near-black ground with warm off-white text, monumental display headings, airy spacing, hairline-ruled tables and ember accents, with coloured light only on 3D surfaces.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the published run manifest on the published port and answers the published health check.

Server boundary
The server enforces the published body-size limits, refuses cross-origin writes, and never serves source files, credentials or configuration.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the published environment variables at start, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Real 3D scenes
The hero, case studies, service objects, process stations and Shot Rig render live WebGL scenes built from procedural primitives and the client's own GLB, with no pre-rendered video standing in for them.

Zero-decimal yen accounts
A JPY account prices, shows, charges in Kill Bill and emails every amount in whole yen with no decimals, using the same conversion, VAT and split rules as the other currencies.

Quantized GLB bounds
A quantized GLB's integer position bounds are dequantized before measurement, and a GLB that requires an unsupported extension or one missing from extensionsUsed is refused with the published copy.

Scheduled exchange rates
A founder-scheduled exchange rate takes effect for unaccepted quotes only from its effective time, and engagements whose deposit is paid keep their locked rate.

Idempotent revision requests
A revision request carries an Idempotency-Key, a replay returns the stored round without counting a second round or adding a second change order, and a key still in flight answers the published 409, as qualified in Business rules.

Refunds across payments and void invoices
A refund is split newest payment first into one Kill Bill refund carrying the published transaction key and one ledger entry per payment it touches, and cancelling voids every unpaid issued invoice and clears the brand's overdue block, as qualified in Business rules.

One cancel wins
Of simultaneous cancellations of one engagement exactly one succeeds, and Kill Bill, the ledger and the inbox hold only that cancellation's refunds and email.

Sign-in code request limit
Each email may request at most three sign-in codes per rolling SIGNIN_CODE_WINDOW_SECONDS, and the fourth answers the published 429 with Retry-After, identically for known and unknown emails.

Abandoned uploads leave nothing
When a client disconnects mid-upload or a file crosses its cap, the server stops reading and within 10 seconds leaves no object, no incomplete multipart upload, no intake file record and no busy database session for that attempt.

Status refresh keeps dialogs intact
The ten-second status refresh shows and clears the outage banner in place without closing an open dialog, clearing typed fields, moving focus or re-announcing unchanged text.

Overdue decided by the server
Invoices carry a server-published overdue_at, and an open invoice page shows Overdue only when a re-read from the server returns it, never from the browser's clock.

Latest quote input wins
Each quote reply carries a revision, the rig applies only a reply newer than the one on screen and rebuilds every rig surface from its lines, including lines written in another tab, so the figures, spinbuttons, frustums and quote live region end on the last input.

Phone navigation drawer
Below 768 pixels the main navigation collapses behind a Menu button whose closed links are hidden and unfocusable, and the open drawer keeps focus inside, closes on Escape and returns focus to Menu.

Renamed shots keep their history
A renamed or repriced shot shows its new title and price on unaccepted quotes, while a deposit-paid engagement keeps its locked title and price on its quote, rig, review stills, invoices and emails.

Refused changes undo what the page showed
A refused quote change flies its frustum back out and restores the rig to the server's quote, a storage outage marks the upload row Not saved, and a billing outage leaves the payment dialog open with its typed values, each announcing the published copy.

Review copies carry only what the reviewer needs
The review-link email, Review JSON, review page and still responses carry only the published reference, brand, milestone and still fields, with no amounts, other contacts' addresses or storage details, and send Referrer-Policy no-referrer.

Reviewer actions at the link's expiry
Reviewer accept and revision requests succeed at exactly REVIEW_LINK_TTL_SECONDS of link age and answer the not-found response after it, replays of stored keys included, counting no round.

One issue per invoice
Of simultaneous issue requests for one invoice exactly one succeeds, and Kill Bill holds one invoice and the finance contact's inbox one invoice email for it, even after a retried issue.

Downloads match the upload
Intake files download from the client and studio routes byte for byte as uploaded, with an RFC 6266 Content-Disposition carrying the exact display name, Japanese names included.

Sign-in lands on the next path
A signed-out visit to a client page signs in and lands on that page, while an off-site, protocol-relative or backslash next path lands on the account page.

Queued intake measurement
Each stored GLB is measured once through one persistent message on the durable intake.measure queue, a redelivered message never measures twice, and a GLB that fails measurement twice moves to intake.measure.dead and shows Rejected.

Measuring queue outage
When RabbitMQ is unreachable, uploads still store and show Received, the model reads Measuring is delayed with the published banner, and no measurement is invented.

PDF receipts and invoices
The deposit receipt and every invoice-issued email attach one Gotenberg-rendered PDF with the published name, holding the reference, lines, VAT, total and locked rate in the account currency's format.

Documents outage
When Gotenberg is unreachable, deposits and invoice issues still complete, their emails wait in the outbox and are never sent without their PDF, and client pages show the published documents banner.

Studio search
The header search queries a Meilisearch index of published case studies, services and insights, a founder publish, edit or unpublish shows in search within 5 seconds, and drafts never appear.

Founder push alerts
The founder's ntfy topic gloamwork-studio receives exactly one push with the published title and message for each deposit paid, revision requested and invoice overdue, never twice for a replayed request.

Service objects tilt toward the pointer
Each Services row's procedural object turns slowly, tilts toward the pointer or on focus by at most 12 degrees, reports the tilt in data-tilt and settles back to 0 when left, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Process camera path
Scrolling through the Process region moves one camera through five 3D stations, with data-process-step from 1 to 5 fixed by scroll position in both directions, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Case study shared-element transition
Opening a case study from the grid morphs the tile's 3D subject into the detail subject in 0.5 to 0.7 seconds with data-transition reading morphing then done, and Back reverses it.

Phone case study deck
Below 768 pixels the public case studies form a 3D card deck that a fast fling, a long drag or the arrow keys advance one card at a time, reported in data-deck-index, while a short slow drag springs back.
/app/run.json holds exactly the string fields _schema (run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve, and serve needs no network install.
App source is TypeScript; JavaScript appears only as build output or tool configuration.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package and every bundled font with name, version and licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Shipped packages carry only MIT, ISC, 0BSD, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause or Apache-2.0 licences, and fonts carry OFL-1.1.

The app keeps state only in the provided services (Postgres, PocketBase, MinIO, Kill Bill, Mailpit, RabbitMQ, Meilisearch, ntfy), with no SQLite, Redis, embedded database, or local files holding app state or uploaded bytes.
The provided service configuration and its dev credentials stay unmodified.
Pages load nothing from third-party origins; fonts, scripts, styles and 3D libraries are served from the app's own origin.
